meta.name: Frontend Product Builder Feedback Components
meta.description: Canonical feedback components for empty, loading, processing, warning, failure, permission, conflict, stale-data, and confirmation states.

EmptyState.name: EmptyState
EmptyState.description: Canonical state for communicating that expected content is absent and guiding the user toward the next valid action.
capabilities: Explain why a collection, region, or workflow has no content.
Distinguish first-use emptiness from filtered no-results state.
Provide an eligible next action without manufacturing urgency.
Preserve the surrounding route and task context.

foundation.reason: Empty states require semantic variants, controlled action hierarchy, content guidance, and responsive composition beyond a generic card.

firstUse.intent: Orient a user before the first resource or record has been created.
allowedUse: A collection has never contained records.
The user can create or configure the missing content.

noResults.intent: Explain that the current search, filters, or scope produced no matching records.
allowedUse: The selected scope contains no matching items.
prohibitedUse: The collection has never contained records.

missingPrerequisite.intent: Explain that content cannot exist until another valid prerequisite is completed.
allowedUse: A document must be uploaded first.
An integration must be connected first.
A parent record must be selected first.

archivedScope.intent: Explain that the current scope intentionally contains no active content because it is archived or inactive.
allowedUse: Closed workflow with no active items.

compact.intent: Region-level empty state inside a table, panel, or subsection.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Optional supporting icon illustrating the empty-state category.
contentRestrictions: The icon must not be the only source of meaning.
Avoid decorative illustrations that consume excessive vertical space.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Concise statement describing the absent content.
contentRestrictions: Do not use generic text such as Nothing here.
Name the missing resource or current result condition.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Explanation of why the state exists and what it means.
contentRestrictions: Do not blame the user.
Do not expose internal query or API details.

slots.name: details
slots.description: Optional supporting context or active-filter summary.
contentRestrictions: Critical recovery information belongs in the description or actions.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Eligible next action or recovery action.
contentRestrictions: One dominant action at most.
Do not show creation actions the user cannot execute.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic reason for the absence of content.
restrictions: The variant must match the actual data condition.

props.name: size
props.description: Region scale of the empty state.
restrictions: Do not use compact only to hide insufficient explanation.

spacingOwnership: EmptyState owns spacing between icon, title, description, details, and actions.
The parent region owns spacing around the complete empty state.
composition.surfaceOwnership: EmptyState may render directly inside the parent or use one subtle surface; it must not introduce nested decorative cards.
rules: Empty is distinct from loading, error, forbidden, and no-results.
The component must not reserve space for absent content outside the empty-state composition.
Action eligibility is supplied by the owning feature.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Explain whether no activity exists or whether a filter removed all data.
First-use and no-results states must be distinct.
Use for missing related records or optional sections.
Invitations, integrations, and roles need capability-aware actions.
Missing evidence and missing recommendation must remain distinct.

notes: The owning query or feature determines why the content is absent.
Actions receive callbacks from the owning feature.

responsive.strategy: Remain centered or start-aligned according to the parent while preserving concise readable text and usable actions.
responsive.compact: Use reduced padding, stack all actions, and avoid large illustrations.
responsive.medium: Use constrained text width and wrapping actions.
responsive.wide: Remain constrained inside the parent region rather than stretching across the route.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not enlarge the illustration or text block to fill space.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Text and actions wrap; no page-level horizontal overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain readable and actionable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: section or status region when the state changes dynamically
keyboard: All recovery and creation actions are keyboard operable.
The empty-state container itself is not focusable by default.
focus: When a loaded collection becomes empty after an action, focus remains in a logical surrounding location.
Route-level navigation may move focus to the title according to application policy.
announcements: Dynamic no-results or empty transitions may use polite status announcements.
Do not repeatedly announce unchanged empty states.
aria: Avoid alert semantics for ordinary empty states.
Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.
accessibility.colorIndependence: The empty-state reason is communicated through text rather than visual tone alone.

content.typical: Title, explanation, optional context, and one eligible action.
content.maximum: A concise task-oriented state; extensive onboarding belongs elsewhere.
content.truncation: Do not truncate the reason or recovery action.
content.localization: Support expanded titles, descriptions, and action labels.
content.emptyBehavior: An EmptyState without a title or explanation is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Query keys, endpoint names, HTTP status codes, and raw filters are prohibited.

ErrorState.name: ErrorState
ErrorState.description: Canonical recoverable or blocking error presentation that communicates operational impact without exposing unsafe implementation details.
capabilities: Explain that a route, region, or operation failed.
Separate recoverable failure from unavailable service or blocked workflow.
Provide retry, return, support, or safe fallback actions.
Expose a safe correlation reference when operationally useful.

foundation.source: Stack, Button, InlineAlert, approved error-normalization contract
foundation.reason: Error presentation requires safe normalized content, recovery hierarchy, correlation references, and scope-aware variants.

region.intent: Communicate a recoverable failure limited to one region while preserving the rest of the screen.
allowedUse: One document could not be loaded.

route.intent: Communicate a failure that prevents the route from fulfilling its primary purpose.
allowedUse: Route prerequisite could not be resolved.

unavailable.intent: Communicate that a required service or dependency is temporarily unavailable.

blocked.intent: Communicate that a workflow cannot continue because a required condition failed.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Optional semantic failure icon.
contentRestrictions: The icon must match the failure severity.
The icon is not the only source of meaning.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Clear statement of what could not be completed.
contentRestrictions: Name the failed task or unavailable content.
Do not use raw exception names.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Safe user-operational explanation and impact.
contentRestrictions: Do not expose stack traces, SQL, internal hosts, secrets, or raw response bodies.

slots.name: reference
slots.description: Optional safe support or correlation reference.
contentRestrictions: Do not expose authentication tokens or database identifiers.
The reference must be safe to copy.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Retry, return, support, or fallback actions.
contentRestrictions: One dominant recovery action.
Do not offer retry when retry cannot change the outcome.

slots.name: details
slots.description: Optional authorized diagnostic disclosure.
contentRestrictions: Visible only to eligible support or administrative roles.
Raw stack traces remain prohibited.

props.name: variant
props.description: Operational scope and meaning of the failure.
restrictions: The variant must reflect the actual failure scope.

props.name: size
props.description: Presentation scale matching the failed region.
restrictions: Do not use compact for route-blocking failures.

spacingOwnership: ErrorState owns spacing between icon, title, description, reference, actions, and authorized details.
The parent region owns spacing around the complete state.
composition.surfaceOwnership: ErrorState may own a semantic danger or warning surface matching the failure scope.
rules: Raw transport errors must be normalized before rendering.
Field validation belongs to FormField or FormErrorSummary.
Retry behavior is supplied by the owning query or feature.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Keep unaffected regions usable.
Do not replace the complete route when only contextual details fail.
Primary entity failure may become route-scoped.
Cross-field and submission errors normally use FormErrorSummary; broader dependency failures may use ErrorState.
Authentication-specific errors require safe account-enumeration behavior.

notes: The owning error boundary, query, mutation, or feature supplies normalized content and recovery callbacks.
Retry, return, copy, and support actions are supplied by feature composition.

responsive.strategy: Preserve the failure explanation and recovery action while constraining technical or supporting details.
responsive.compact: Stack title, explanation, reference, and actions.
responsive.medium: Use constrained text width and wrapping actions.
responsive.wide: Remain aligned with the failed region rather than stretching across unrelated content.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not increase content width merely to fill the viewport.
responsive.overflowPolicy: References wrap or use safe copy controls; no page-level horizontal overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain readable and actionable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: alert for newly surfaced blocking errors or labeled section for persistent route errors
keyboard: All recovery actions are keyboard operable.
Authorized details disclosure is keyboard operable.
focus: The owning workflow may move focus to a newly rendered blocking error.
Do not repeatedly steal focus during automatic retries.
announcements: New blocking failures use assertive or appropriate alert semantics.
Persistent route errors are not repeatedly announced.
aria: Use role=alert only when immediate announcement is justified.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Failure meaning is communicated through title, description, and icon in addition to color.

content.minimum: A specific failure title and safe explanation.
content.typical: Title, impact explanation, one recovery action, and optional reference.
content.maximum: A concise operational explanation with authorized progressive diagnostic disclosure.
content.wrapping: All text and references wrap safely.
content.truncation: Do not truncate the failure impact or required recovery steps.
content.localization: Support expanded error and action text.
content.emptyBehavior: An ErrorState without an explanation is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Only safe correlation references and approved diagnostic summaries are allowed.

LoadingState.name: LoadingState
LoadingState.description: Canonical initial-loading and local-pending presentation that preserves expected geometry and communicates that content is being retrieved.
capabilities: Represent initial loading for a route, region, or component.
Compose realistic skeleton structures.
Communicate pending status to assistive technology.
Distinguish initial loading from background refreshing and long-running processing.

foundation.source: Skeleton, native status semantics, approved progress indicator
foundation.reason: Loading requires scope-aware geometry, announcement behavior, reduced-motion handling, and separation from background refresh.

skeleton.intent: Preserve the geometry of content that has not yet loaded.
prohibitedUse: Background refresh when usable data already exists.

inline.intent: Communicate a small local pending state without replacing surrounding content.
prohibitedUse: Primary mutation submission when a button pending state is sufficient.

route.intent: Represent an unresolved route prerequisite or initial route payload.

refreshing.intent: Indicate background synchronization while preserving existing content.
prohibitedUse: Blocking the complete route without necessity.

compact.intent: Local pending indicator or compact region skeleton.

default.intent: Major region or route loading composition.

slots.name: indicator
slots.description: Skeleton composition or approved local loading indicator.
contentRestrictions: The structure should approximate eventual content.
Do not use decorative animation without loading meaning.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Optional visible loading description when useful.
contentRestrictions: Use concise task-specific wording.
Do not promise a completion time without evidence.

props.name: variant
props.description: Loading scope and presentation strategy.
restrictions: Use refreshing when existing data remains usable.

props.name: size
props.description: Scale matching the loading scope.
restrictions: Do not use a route-size loading state inside a small panel.

prohibitedParents: Button when Button loading is sufficient
spacingOwnership: LoadingState owns spacing between loading indicators and optional visible label.
The skeleton composition owns spacing among placeholder shapes.
composition.surfaceOwnership: LoadingState normally inherits the eventual content surface.
rules: Initial loading, refreshing, and long-running processing are distinct.
Skeletons approximate final geometry.
Existing usable data remains visible during background refresh.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Each region receives a realistic loading shape.
Initial table loading differs from background refetch.
Primary entity orientation must not render incomplete placeholder values as final data.
Edit forms initialize only after authoritative data is available.
Protected application content must not flash before session resolution.

notes: The owning query, route, or feature decides when the loading state renders.

responsive.strategy: Mirror the responsive structure of the eventual content and avoid introducing temporary overflow.
responsive.compact: Use compact target geometry and reduced placeholder count.
responsive.wide: Approximate the approved wide content structure.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not create additional placeholders absent from the eventual layout.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Skeletons and indicators must not create page-level horizontal overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Loading status remains perceivable with enlarged text and reduced motion.

accessibility.semanticElement: status region or container using aria-busy
accessibility.accessibleName: Visible or visually hidden task-specific loading label.
keyboard: Previously usable controls remain operable during non-blocking refresh where safe.
focus: Initial loading must not move focus into decorative skeletons.
Background refresh must not reset focus.
announcements: Initial pending state may be announced politely.
Do not repeatedly announce frequent background refreshes.
Completion is announced only when operationally useful.
aria: Use aria-busy on the appropriate region.
Hide decorative skeleton shapes from assistive technology.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Loading meaning is communicated through status semantics or text, not animation or color alone.
accessibility.contrastTarget: WCAG 2.2 AA for visible labels and meaningful indicators

content.typical: A realistic skeleton composition and optional visible label.
content.maximum: Only enough placeholders to preserve expected geometry.
content.truncation: Do not truncate required loading context.
content.emptyBehavior: A LoadingState without an accessible pending indication is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Query keys, endpoint names, and transport state labels are prohibited.

PermissionState.name: PermissionState
PermissionState.description: Canonical presentation for unavailable capabilities, restricted content, read-only access, and actions disabled by authorization policy.
capabilities: Communicate that a capability or content region is unavailable to the current user.
Distinguish hidden, forbidden, read-only, and disabled-with-reason behaviors.
Explain valid next steps without disclosing protected information.
Preserve safe surrounding context when policy permits.

foundation.reason: Permission outcomes require consistent disclosure, safe messaging, action eligibility, and region- versus route-level behavior.

forbidden.intent: Block access to a route or region while revealing only approved context.
allowedUse: The user lacks a required capability.
The user cannot access the requested tenant or entity.
A protected administrative area is unavailable.
User may view but not edit.
Record is locked by workflow state.
prohibitedUse: User cannot view the content at all.
Editable controls merely failed to load.

disabledWithReason.intent: Explain why a visible action or capability is currently ineligible.
allowedUse: Current workflow state blocks the action.
User capability exists but temporary eligibility does not.
prohibitedUse: The user must not know the action exists.
The reason is a technical backend failure.

restrictedData.intent: Indicate that part of otherwise accessible content is intentionally withheld.

inline.intent: Small explanation adjacent to a disabled or read-only capability.

region.intent: Restricted section or major feature area.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Clear statement of the access or eligibility condition.
contentRestrictions: Do not disclose protected resource existence when policy forbids it.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Safe explanation of the current capability state.
contentRestrictions: Do not expose internal role names or permission implementation.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Approved return, request-access, or prerequisite action.
contentRestrictions: Request-access actions require an actual supported workflow.
Do not offer privilege escalation as an immediate action.

props.name: variant
props.description: Permission or eligibility presentation policy.
restrictions: The variant must follow the approved disclosure policy.

props.name: size
props.description: Scope of the restricted capability.
restrictions: Route-level restrictions must not use inline presentation.

prohibitedParents: Badge as the complete permission message
spacingOwnership: PermissionState owns spacing between title, description, and actions.
The owning region controls surrounding spacing.
composition.surfaceOwnership: PermissionState may own a subtle informational or warning surface according to scope.
rules: Capability evaluation occurs outside the component.
The backend remains authoritative.
Hidden versus visible restricted behavior follows an explicit disclosure policy.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Row actions may be hidden or disabled according to disclosure policy.
View and edit capabilities remain distinct.
Read-only presentation should not misuse disabled inputs.
Administration uses capability-oriented checks rather than visible role-name comparisons.
Review may remain read-only when decision capability is absent.

notes: The owning feature supplies the resolved permission outcome and safe user-facing content.
Return or access-request callbacks are supplied externally.

responsive.strategy: Preserve the access explanation and safe next action without occupying excessive route space.
responsive.wide: Remain aligned to the restricted region.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not stretch across unrelated route content.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain understandable and actionable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: section, note, or status region according to scope
keyboard: Available return or request actions are keyboard operable.
Restricted controls must not remain accidentally focusable.
focus: Route-level forbidden states may receive route-entry focus according to application policy.
Read-only regions preserve logical reading order.
announcements: A newly changed eligibility state may be announced politely.
aria: Disabled controls use native disabled semantics when appropriate.
Read-only controls and read-only content remain semantically distinct.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Restriction, read-only, and disabled meaning are communicated through text and semantics in addition to color.

content.typical: Access condition, impact, and optional valid next action.
content.maximum: A concise explanation; complete authorization policy belongs in documentation.
content.truncation: Do not truncate the restriction reason.
content.emptyBehavior: PermissionState without a clear access condition is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Internal role codes, policy object keys, capability IDs, and authorization implementation are prohibited.

InlineAlert.name: InlineAlert
InlineAlert.description: Canonical inline semantic message for informational, success, warning, and danger feedback within the current workflow context.
capabilities: Communicate contextual information, success, warning, or error.
Provide concise supporting actions.
Render static or dynamically announced feedback.
Preserve semantic hierarchy without opening a modal.

foundation.source: Native status and alert semantics, Stack, Button
foundation.reason: Inline feedback requires semantic tone, announcement policy, action hierarchy, and consistent anatomy.

info.intent: Communicate neutral operational information or guidance.

success.intent: Communicate a completed or healthy outcome.

warning.intent: Communicate attention, risk, incomplete state, or non-blocking conflict.

danger.intent: Communicate an error, blocking risk, destructive impact, or failed state.

compact.intent: Concise message inside a local component or field group.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Optional semantic icon.
contentRestrictions: Icon tone must match the selected variant.
Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Optional concise message heading.
contentRestrictions: Required when the description is complex or the state is critical.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Primary message content.
contentRestrictions: Do not expose raw server or security details.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Optional local recovery or contextual actions.
contentRestrictions: One dominant action at most.
Avoid several unrelated actions.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic message tone.
restrictions: Do not select based only on preferred color.

props.name: size
props.description: Message density matching the containing region.
restrictions: Compact messages still require complete meaning.

props.name: announcement
props.description: Announcement policy for dynamically inserted feedback.
restrictions: Static informational content normally uses none.
Assertive announcements are reserved for urgent blocking changes.

spacingOwnership: InlineAlert owns spacing among icon, title, description, and actions.
The parent owns spacing around the alert.
composition.surfaceOwnership: InlineAlert owns its semantic message surface.
rules: Static and dynamically announced alerts use different announcement policies.
Do not use toasts as a replacement for persistent actionable errors.
The variant communicates meaning rather than decoration.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Critical attention uses warning or danger semantics.
Form-level failure and field errors remain distinct.
Danger alerts accompany sensitive-action impact.
Messages must follow account-enumeration policy.
Recommendation limitations and blocking conflicts remain explicit.

prohibited: Determining message severity from raw HTTP status.

notes: The owning workflow selects the semantic variant and announcement policy.

responsive.strategy: Preserve message meaning and action visibility while stacking internal regions when space decreases.
responsive.compact: Icon, text, and actions stack or align at the start.
responsive.wide: Actions may align beside concise content.
responsive.ultrawide: Message width remains constrained by its parent.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Long messages and actions wrap; no horizontal overflow.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain readable and actionable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: status, alert, or neutral section according to announcement policy
accessibility.accessibleName: Visible title when present, otherwise message text.
keyboard: The alert container is not focusable unless focus is explicitly required.
focus: Blocking form errors may receive focus through the owning workflow.
Informational alerts do not steal focus.
announcements: Urgent blocking messages may use alert semantics.
Static content uses no live announcement by default.
aria: Do not combine redundant role=alert and assertive live-region behavior.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Message type is communicated through text, icon, and semantics in addition to color.

content.typical: Optional title, concise explanation, and one contextual action.
content.maximum: A focused operational message; extensive documentation belongs elsewhere.
content.truncation: Do not truncate warnings, errors, or required actions.
content.localization: Support expanded labels and message text.
content.emptyBehavior: An InlineAlert without message content is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Raw errors, stack traces, query keys, tokens, and internal response bodies are prohibited.

ConfirmationDialog.name: ConfirmationDialog
ConfirmationDialog.description: Canonical modal confirmation for consequential actions, including impact explanation, semantic action hierarchy, pending state, and optional elevated verification.
capabilities: Require explicit confirmation before a consequential action.
Explain scope, impact, reversibility, and affected object.
Separate ordinary, destructive, and sensitive confirmations.
Prevent duplicate execution while confirmation is pending.

foundation.reason: Consequential confirmations require consistent impact wording, button semantics, focus behavior, pending orchestration, and optional reauthentication or typed confirmation.

ordinary.intent: Confirm a consequential but reversible or non-destructive action.

destructive.intent: Confirm deletion, revocation, disabling, or another materially destructive action.

sensitive.intent: Confirm an action requiring elevated awareness, reauthentication, or additional verification.

lg.intent: Complex impact summary or required confirmation input.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Question naming the action and affected object.
contentRestrictions: Use explicit action and object names.
Avoid generic Are you sure wording as the complete title.

slots.name: impact
slots.description: Explanation of scope, consequence, and reversibility.
contentRestrictions: State whether the action is reversible.
Do not hide critical impact in a tooltip.

slots.name: affectedObject
slots.description: Optional identity summary of the affected record, account, tenant, or resource.
contentRestrictions: Avoid ambiguous references such as this item when identity matters.

slots.name: verification
slots.description: Optional typed confirmation, acknowledgement, rationale, or reauthentication step.
contentRestrictions: Use only when justified by risk policy.
Do not create friction merely for visual seriousness.

slots.name: error
slots.description: Normalized mutation or verification failure.
contentRestrictions: Preserve the dialog and entered verification values after recoverable failure.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Cancel and semantic confirmation actions.
contentRestrictions: One confirmation action and one cancel action.
Destructive confirmation uses the danger variant.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic consequence level of the confirmation.
restrictions: Variant must follow actual action impact.

props.name: size
props.description: Dialog size based on impact and verification complexity.
restrictions: Do not use lg merely to create visual importance.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled modal visibility.
restrictions: The owning feature controls visibility.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Controlled visibility callback.
restrictions: Pending behavior may prevent accidental dismissal according to policy.

props.name: loading
props.description: Indicates that final confirmation is being processed.
restrictions: Must prevent duplicate confirmation.

prohibitedParents: Another modal dialog without explicit nested-flow approval
spacingOwnership: ConfirmationDialog owns spacing between title, impact, object summary, verification, error, and actions.
Dialog foundation owns overlay and modal positioning.
composition.surfaceOwnership: ConfirmationDialog owns the elevated modal surface and semantic impact treatment.
rules: The affected object and consequence are explicit.
Destructive confirmation never uses the ordinary primary button variant.
Mutation execution remains owned by the feature.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Use for discard, conflict, or consequential save confirmation.
Deletion and irreversible entity actions require explicit impact.
May include reauthentication or typed confirmation.
Use only when decision policy requires final confirmation.

notes: Visibility and pending state are controlled by the owning feature.
Verification form state may be owned by an approved nested form composition.
Dialog foundation traps focus and locks background scroll.
The confirmation callback owns the mutation.

responsive.strategy: Constrain modal width and preserve impact, verification, errors, and actions within the viewport.
responsive.compact: Use near-full-width presentation, stacked actions, and internal scrolling only when required.
responsive.medium: Centered constrained dialog with wrapping action footer.
responsive.ultrawide: Remain constrained and do not enlarge with the viewport.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Long impact content scrolls inside the modal while title and actions remain accessible.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain operable at 200% text scaling.

keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab remain inside the dialog.
Escape closes only when policy allows dismissal.
Confirmation and cancellation are keyboard operable.
focus: Initial focus normally targets the safest non-destructive action or first required verification control.
Focus returns to the trigger after close.
announcements: Title and impact description are announced on open.
Mutation failure and pending state are perceivable.
aria: Destructive meaning is not communicated through aria labels alone.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Consequence is communicated through explicit text, action label, and icon in addition to color.

content.minimum: Explicit action, affected object or scope, impact, cancel action, and confirmation action.
content.typical: Title, consequence explanation, affected-object summary, optional verification, and two actions.
content.maximum: A bounded impact and verification workflow; complete configuration belongs on a route.
content.wrapping: All impact, labels, and actions wrap safely.
content.truncation: Do not truncate affected identity or consequence.
content.localization: Support expanded titles, impact statements, and actions.
content.emptyBehavior: A confirmation without impact explanation is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Raw mutation errors, API routes, permission keys, and internal identifiers are prohibited.

ProcessingState.name: ProcessingState
ProcessingState.description: Canonical state for long-running domain operations that continue beyond a single request and may expose progress, stages, cancellation, retry, or background continuation.
capabilities: Communicate that a domain operation is still running.
Present determinate or indeterminate progress without inventing precision.
Expose current stage, elapsed context, and safe next actions.
Distinguish queued, running, delayed, completed, failed, and unavailable conditions.

foundation.source: Native progress semantics, Stack, Button, InlineAlert
foundation.reason: Long-running operations require explicit progress truthfulness, stage semantics, background behavior, and recovery states.

queued.intent: Communicate that an operation has been accepted but has not begun execution.

indeterminate.intent: Communicate active processing when reliable percentage progress is unavailable.

determinate.intent: Communicate measurable progress from an authoritative source.
prohibitedUse: Progress based only on elapsed animation.

delayed.intent: Communicate that processing continues but is taking longer than expected.

failed.intent: Communicate that a background operation ended unsuccessfully.
prohibitedUse: Initial query failed before a process existed.

completed.intent: Communicate verified completion and expose the resulting next action.
allowedUse: Processing result is authoritative and available.
prohibitedUse: Machine recommendation is awaiting human review.
Completion has not been confirmed by the backend.

inline.intent: Compact processing context embedded near an affected item.

route.intent: Primary route represents the running process.

slots.name: status
slots.description: Visible current process state.
contentRestrictions: Use user-facing process terminology.
Do not expose internal queue codes.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Task-oriented process description.
contentRestrictions: Describe what is being processed.

slots.name: progress
slots.description: Authoritative percentage or indeterminate progress indicator.
contentRestrictions: Do not display a percentage unless it is authoritative.
Do not animate fabricated progress.

slots.name: stage
slots.description: Optional current stage or processing explanation.
contentRestrictions: Translate internal stage keys into user-facing language.

slots.name: message
slots.description: Optional delay, failure, completion, or background-continuation message.
contentRestrictions: Do not guarantee completion time without an authoritative estimate.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Cancel, retry, continue in background, view result, or return actions.
contentRestrictions: Actions must be supported by the process contract.
Cancellation must explain whether work already completed is reversible.

props.name: variant
props.type: queued | indeterminate | determinate | delayed | failed | completed
props.description: Authoritative lifecycle state of the process.
restrictions: Do not infer completed from local timer or animation.

props.name: size
props.description: Process-state presentation scope.
restrictions: The size must match the affected workflow region.

props.name: progress
props.description: Authoritative progress percentage from 0 to 100 or null when indeterminate.
restrictions: Required for determinate variant.
Must not be estimated by presentation code.

prohibitedParents: Button when local loading is sufficient
spacingOwnership: ProcessingState owns spacing among status, title, progress, stage, message, and actions.
The parent region owns surrounding layout.
composition.surfaceOwnership: ProcessingState may own a contextual process surface matching its scope.
rules: Loading data and processing a domain operation are distinct.
Determinate progress requires an authoritative value.
Completed status requires backend-confirmed completion.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Rows may expose processing status without replacing the collection.
Documents and imports may continue asynchronously.
Ordinary submission pending normally remains inside FormActionBar.
Pending analysis must not be presented as final recommendation.
Integration checks, imports, and key rotation may be asynchronous.

notes: The owning feature or query supplies the authoritative process lifecycle and callbacks.
Cancel, retry, and view-result actions are supplied externally.

responsive.strategy: Preserve process identity, current state, and next action while stacking supporting metadata.
responsive.compact: Stack progress, stage, messages, and actions.
responsive.medium: Use constrained process content and wrapping actions.
responsive.wide: Status and primary metadata may align horizontally.
responsive.ultrawide: Do not enlarge progress visuals merely to fill space.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Stage and message content wrap; long identifiers remain hidden or safely copyable through approved metadata components.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain understandable and operable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: status region with native progress semantics when determinate
keyboard: All cancel, retry, background, and result actions are keyboard operable.
focus: Status updates do not repeatedly steal focus.
Failure recovery may move focus according to the owning workflow.
announcements: Meaningful stage changes may be announced politely.
Failure and completion are announced once when operationally useful.
Frequent percentage updates should not produce excessive announcements.
aria: Use native progress element when appropriate.
Expose indeterminate progress without fabricated aria-valuenow.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Queued, running, delayed, failed, and completed states use text and semantics in addition to color.

content.minimum: Process title and current lifecycle state.
content.typical: Title, status, progress or stage, supporting message, and optional actions.
content.maximum: A concise process summary; detailed logs belong in authorized diagnostics.
content.wrapping: All status text and actions wrap.
content.truncation: Do not truncate failure or cancellation consequences.
content.localization: Support expanded process and stage labels.
content.emptyBehavior: ProcessingState without an authoritative lifecycle state is invalid.
content.technicalContent: Raw queue names, job payloads, worker IDs, stack traces, and internal stage codes are prohibited.

StaleDataNotice.name: StaleDataNotice
StaleDataNotice.description: Canonical feedback for outdated, superseded, or conflicting data that may require refresh, comparison, or reconciliation before continuing.
capabilities: Communicate that visible data may no longer be authoritative.
Distinguish non-blocking staleness from blocking conflict.
Provide refresh, compare, reload, or preserve-local-changes actions.
Prevent silent submission against outdated evidence or configuration.

foundation.reason: Stale-data handling requires explicit blocking policy, freshness context, conflict messaging, and controlled recovery actions.

nonBlocking.intent: Warn that data is older than preferred but remains usable.
allowedUse: Dashboard data passed its freshness threshold.
Background refresh failed while existing data remains valid enough.

blocking.intent: Block an action until the user reloads or reviews newer authoritative data.
allowedUse: Edit version no longer matches the server.
Configuration changed while the user was editing.

conflict.intent: Communicate that local changes and newer server values require explicit reconciliation.
allowedUse: Dirty form conflicts with updated server record.
Decision draft conflicts with changed evidence.
prohibitedUse: Automatic safe refresh without local changes.

superseded.intent: Communicate that the current record, recommendation, or version was replaced by a newer authoritative version.
prohibitedUse: Current version is merely old but still authoritative.

inline.intent: Compact notice near an affected value or panel.

region.intent: Major warning affecting a workflow region.

slots.name: title
slots.description: Clear statement that the visible data is outdated, changed, or superseded.
contentRestrictions: State whether the user may safely continue.

slots.name: description
slots.description: Impact and required reconciliation explanation.
contentRestrictions: Do not expose raw version tokens.

slots.name: freshness
slots.description: Optional current-data timestamp or freshness context.
contentRestrictions: Dates follow the project localization and time-zone policy.

slots.name: comparison
slots.description: Optional concise summary or entry point for comparing local and current values.
contentRestrictions: Do not hide material changes behind an unlabeled icon.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Refresh, reload, compare, preserve, discard, or retry actions.
contentRestrictions: One dominant resolution action.
Actions must explain the effect on unsaved work.

props.name: variant
props.description: Operational impact of the stale state.
restrictions: Blocking variants require enforced action eligibility outside the component.

props.name: size
props.description: Scope of the stale-data condition.
restrictions: Conflict affecting submission normally uses region size.

prohibitedParents: Tooltip as the only stale-data explanation
Badge as the complete conflict state
spacingOwnership: StaleDataNotice owns spacing between title, description, freshness, comparison, and actions.
The parent owns spacing around the notice.
composition.surfaceOwnership: StaleDataNotice owns a warning or danger semantic surface matching the impact.
rules: The notice does not enforce version checks; the owning feature does.
Blocking stale state must also disable or reject unsafe submission.
Unsaved values are preserved until the user explicitly chooses a resolution.

recipeCompatibility.notes: Dashboard staleness is normally non-blocking and includes freshness context.
Preserve visible data during failed background refresh.
Editing conflicts require explicit reconciliation.
Dirty values must not be silently reset.
Changed evidence blocks final decision until reviewed again.

notes: The owning feature supplies the resolved stale condition, impact, freshness, and actions.
Refresh, compare, reload, and conflict actions are supplied externally.

responsive.strategy: Preserve conflict impact and resolution actions while stacking freshness and comparison context.
responsive.compact: Stack explanation, freshness, comparison, and actions.
responsive.medium: Use constrained text and wrapping actions.
responsive.wide: Freshness may align beside concise explanation.
responsive.ultrawide: Remain aligned to the affected workflow region.
responsive.overflowPolicy: Dates, labels, and actions wrap; raw version identifiers are not displayed.
responsive.zoomExpectation: Must remain understandable and actionable at 200% text scaling.

accessibility.semanticElement: alert for newly surfaced blocking conflict or status region for non-blocking staleness
keyboard: All resolution actions are keyboard operable.
Comparison disclosure or dialog is keyboard operable.
focus: A newly blocking conflict may receive focus through the owning workflow.
Non-blocking freshness updates do not steal focus.
announcements: Blocking conflict is announced assertively or appropriately.
Background freshness changes use polite or no announcement according to operational importance.
aria: Do not expose raw version data through accessible labels.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Stale, blocking, conflict, and superseded states use text, icon, and semantics in addition to color.

content.minimum: A stale-data statement, impact explanation, and valid resolution action.
content.typical: Title, explanation, freshness context, and refresh or compare action.
content.maximum: A concise conflict summary; complete differences belong in a dedicated comparison component.
content.truncation: Do not truncate conflict impact or resolution consequences.
content.localization: Support expanded conflict and action text.
content.emptyBehavior: StaleDataNotice without an explicit stale condition is invalid.
content.technicalContent: ETags, hashes, revision IDs, database timestamps, and raw concurrency errors are prohibited.

checks.description: The feedback component catalog must validate against the component catalog schema.
checks.remediation: Correct invalid or missing feedback component fields.

checks.description: Feedback components must not duplicate canonical IDs, names, implementations, public imports, or semantic responsibilities.
checks.remediation: Resolve duplicate feedback ownership or merge overlapping contracts.

checks.description: Shared feedback components must not parse transport errors, execute queries, invoke mutations, or evaluate permissions.
checks.remediation: Move state interpretation and side effects to the owning feature, query, mutation, or permission layer.

checks.description: Dynamic feedback must use an explicit announcement strategy and must not create duplicate or excessive live-region output.
checks.remediation: Correct role, aria-live, focus, or announcement behavior.

checks.description: Empty, loading, error, unavailable, forbidden, stale, processing, and success states must remain semantically distinct.
checks.remediation: Correct the state mapping and select the canonical component matching the actual condition.

checks.description: Raw errors, stack traces, tokens, hashes, internal role names, query keys, and unsafe implementation details must not appear in ordinary feedback.
checks.remediation: Normalize technical information through the approved frontend error, permission, and diagnostic layers.

checks.description: Feedback components must remain readable, actionable, and free from horizontal overflow at approved compact, desktop, and zoom scenarios.
checks.remediation: Correct wrapping, action stacking, modal dimensions, or container behavior.

checks.description: Page-local alert, error, empty, loading, permission, processing, and confirmation implementations similar to canonical components require review.
checks.remediation: Reuse the canonical feedback component or document why the local composition is semantically distinct.
